thread:
matt_sales: Fyi, Prospect 'Crane Inc' POC on Dedicated is seeing intermittent 429s + elevated TTFT this morning. Can eng take a quick look?

emmie_se: Can you share the SDK version and one sample Request-ID? Also what model/region are they using?

matt_sales: JS SDK v0.9.3, region eu-west-1, model=redwood-medium-1. Sample header: 
```
Request-ID: req_cc12f1
session_id: session-temp-78
prompt_tokens: ~240
```

matt_sales: UX shows first token ~900-1600ms intermittently; they also reported 4xx spam of 429s in their app logs.

sanjay_infra: Pulling pool logs for dedicated-eu-west-1. Found bunch of queue spikes and CACHE_MISS markers. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-21T08:21:10Z] req=req_cc12f1 pool=dedicated-eu-west-1 queued=1 latency_ms=1800 error=RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
[2026-03-21T08:21:11Z] pool=d-eu-w1 concurrency=46 max=48 queue_len=92
[2026-03-21T08:21:12Z] kv_cache_hit=false kv_hit_rate=18% batching_group=mixed
```

sanjay_infra: Looks like pool is near max concurrency and lots of mixing short vs long prompts in same batch. KV cache hit rate is low (sub 20%).

leah_devex: Low kv_hit_rate + I see their session_id pattern is session-temp-XX per call 12. That will bust prefix/KV caching. They probably rotate session for perceived security.

emmie_se: If we can't change customer behavior quickly, any short-term server-side knobs?

sanjay_infra: Quick mitigations I can push: reduce max_concurrency from 48 -> 32 for that pool (to reduce OOM/queue thrashing), enable prefix_cache for dedicated-eu-west-1, and enable batch segregation so long requests (>1024 tokens) don't get bundled with many short requests. Proposed config (applied as hotfix): 
```json
{
  "pool": "dedicated-eu-west-1",
  "max_concurrency": 32,
  "prefix_cache": true,
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
    "max_batch_size": 10,
    "segregate_long_prompts": true
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config-update OK 10 by sanjay_infra. ticket=RW-17890.

leah_devex: For the customer, best practice: surface session affinity as a recommended change in SDK docs and suggest using a stable session_id per conversation. It's purely a client-side change, no extra data residency implication.

matt_sales: They'll want to know how this impacts billing if we cap concurrency or they have retries. Can we estimate?

leah_devex: Rough back-of-envelope: Their observed token throughput pre-fix ~1800 tokens/sec. With batching segregation + prefix cache on, expected throughput to normalize to ~1100-1300 tokens/sec but with much lower latency variability. If we instead tried to keep 1800 by adding burst capacity, POC reserved costs could rise ~+$150/day during the trial. If we cap concurrency, throughput drops which reduces cost but may affect SLA during peak tests. I'll send the calc to @matt_sales.

emmie_se: I'll ask the customer to switch to a per-conversation session_id before our 10:30 CET sync. Also will test their SDK to ensure it persists session_id between messages.

sanjay_infra: Long term action items: 1) lib change to make session affinity recommended/default in JS SDK; 2) runtime heuristic to split batches by expected completion time; 3) add KV_hit_rate < 35% alert for SEs. I'll open PRs and link.

matt_sales: Thanks team. I'll update Crane Inc and confirm the 10:30 sync. Please ping here if you see residual 429s after the config change. :thumbsup:
